title: Policybazaar parent PB Fintech's profit jumps 92% to Rs 163 crore in Q1 FY27
summary:
PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar announced its Q1 FY27 results today. The company reported a 92% year-on-year jump in profit after tax to Rs 163 crore.
The Gurugram-based company posted operating revenue of Rs 1,888 crore in Q1 FY27, a 40% increase from Rs 1,348 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, as per the firm’s financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Revenue from the core online business was led by Policybazaar, which contributed Rs 1,067 crore, while Paisabazaar added Rs 127 crore. The company's new initiatives, including PB Partners, PB for Business, PB UAE and PB Connect, collectively generated Rs 694 crore.
In addition to operating revenue, the firm earned Rs 93 crore from interest and gains on financial assets during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 1,981 crore for the quarter ended March 2026.
On a quarterly basis, PB Fintech’s revenue dropped over 8% from Rs 2,061 crore in Q4 FY26.
The company's total insurance premium rose 41% year-on-year to Rs 8,372 crore during the quarter, led by a 53% increase in new protection premium, including a 59% growth in health insurance premium. 
Employee benefit expenses remained the group's largest cost, accounting for 40% of total expenditure at Rs 716 crore, a 28% increase from the year-ago quarter. Advertising and promotional expenses also climbed 50% year-on-year to Rs 379 crore in Q1 FY27.
The company did not provide a detailed breakup of other expenses in its quarterly financials. Overall expenditure rose 33% year-on-year to Rs 1,800 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,356 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Coming to the bottom line, the group's profit after tax surged 92% year-on-year to Rs 163 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 85 crore in the same quarter last year, led by a 41% year-on-year growth in insurance premium.
However, on a sequential basis, PB Fintech's profit declined more than 37% from Rs 261 crore in Q4 FY26.
At the end of today’s trading session, shares of PB Fintech closed at Rs 1,620, taking its total market capitalization to Rs 74,957 crore (about $7.89 billion).

title: River Mobility raises $120 Mn in Series C led by Elev8, Claypond Capital
summary:
Electric two wheeler maker River Mobility has raised $120 million in a Series C funding round comprising equity and venture debt, one of the largest private funding rounds in India's electric two wheeler segment.
The equity round was led by Elev8 Venture Partners and Claypond Capital, with participation from Singularity AMC, Anicut Capital, 360 ONE Asset, JIF Capital and HDFC AMC. Existing investors including Yamaha Motor Corporation, Al Futtaim Group and Mitsui & Co also participated, while Alteria Capital, Innoven Capital and Stride Ventures joined through venture debt.
Founded in 2021 by Aravind Mani and Vipin George, River Mobility manufactures electric two wheelers with a focus on utility oriented products. Its flagship electric scooter, Indie, was launched in 2023.
The company will use the fresh capital to expand capacity at its existing manufacturing facility, set up a new greenfield plant, launch new products in the utility lifestyle segment, and improve gross margins and EBITDA profitability.
"This funding marks an important milestone in River's journey. The confidence shown by both our existing and new investors reinforces our belief that there is tremendous opportunity to build India's first utility and design based mobility brand," said Aravind Mani, co-founder and CEO of River Mobility.
River currently operates more than 75 retail stores across India and plans to expand its network to over 350 stores by March 2028.
According to the company, monthly sales have reached around 5,000 units over the past year as it continues to expand its manufacturing capacity and distribution network. It also plans to introduce new electric vehicle models over the coming years.
In February 2024, River raised $40 million in a Series B funding round led by Yamaha, with participation from Al Futtaim Group, Lowercarbon Capital, Toyota Ventures and Maniv Mobility. Prior to that, it had secured $15 million in a Series A round in June 2023.
With the latest financing, River has raised around $188 million across equity and venture debt since its inception. The latest round also marks the company's first major backing from Indian institutional investors, adding to its existing global investor base that includes Yamaha Motor Corporation, Marubeni Corporation, Mitsui & Co, Al Futtaim Group, Lowercarbon Capital, Toyota Ventures, Maniv Mobility and Trucks VC.

title: Swiggy outlines exclusive product strategy for Instamart, sees cash break-even in two quarters
summary:
While Swiggy's quarterly results highlighted continued investments in quick commerce, the company's earnings call offered fresh insight into how it plans to differentiate Instamart in an increasingly competitive market. Rather than focusing only on network expansion, management outlined a strategy centred on exclusive products, private labels and brand partnerships, while reiterating its path towards cash break-even over the next two quarters.
A key announcement during the call was the launch of "Switch to Better", an initiative aimed at offering differentiated products on Instamart. According to management, the programme brings together large FMCG companies, challenger brands and Swiggy's own private labels to develop products that are available only on the platform.
The company said exclusivity often extends to individual SKUs rather than entire brands. For example, multiple high-protein oat variants have been developed exclusively for Instamart, while some brands offer exclusive pricing on the platform. In categories such as eggs, Swiggy is promoting its own private label. Management said the objective is to provide customers with better products at competitive prices.
Executives also indicated that the strategy is category-specific. Depending on the segment, Instamart works with established FMCG brands, emerging direct-to-consumer companies or its own private labels. The company believes this approach can help build differentiation as competition in quick commerce intensifies.
Beyond merchandising, Swiggy shared an update on profitability. Chief Financial Officer Rahul Bothra said improving margins in the food delivery business and treasury income are expected to help the company achieve overall cash break-even within the next two quarters, even as investments in quick commerce continue.
Management also outlined its capital allocation framework for new businesses. It said emerging initiatives are first evaluated for product-market fit and business-market fit before receiving additional investment. Once those milestones are achieved, businesses are expected to scale with clear unit economics rather than relying on continued capital deployment.
The company added that it will share more details on its broader strategy during its upcoming Investor Day.
The earnings call suggests Swiggy is gradually moving beyond competing only on delivery speed. While rapid fulfillment remains the foundation of Instamart, the company's next phase appears to hinge on offering products that customers cannot easily find elsewhere. Through exclusive SKUs, private labels and brand partnerships, Swiggy is attempting to build a differentiated shopping experience that can improve customer retention and margins as competition in quick commerce intensifies.

title: Tracxn slips into loss as revenue remains flat in Q1 FY27
summary:
Data intelligence platform Tracxn announced its Q1 FY27 results on Wednesday. The Bengaluru-based company reported flat revenue during the quarter, while it slipped into losses.

Tracxn’s revenue from operations declined 0.6% to Rs 21.08 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 21.20 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal (Q1 FY26), according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Tracxn derived its entire operating revenue from subscription sales that provide access to its data and software. However, the company did not disclose a detailed revenue breakup for the quarter.
The company also earned Rs 1.52 crore from non operating sources, taking its total revenue to Rs 22.60 crore in the first quarter of FY27.
Employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost head, increasing 16% to Rs 21.98 crore and accounting for 86.64% of the overall expenditure during the quarter. The company’s total expenses rose 18.4% to Rs 25.37 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 21.43 crore in Q1 FY26.
Due to the sharp increase in expenses, Tracxn reported a loss of Rs 3.01 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to a profit of Rs 1.12 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On a quarter on quarter basis, Tracxn reported a marginal 2.9% growth in operating revenue to Rs 21.08 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 20.49 crore in Q4 FY26. However, its losses widened 14.4% to Rs 3.01 crore during the same period from Rs 2.63 crore in the preceding quarter.
At the close of trading on Monday, Tracxn's shares settled at Rs 30.62, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately Rs 319 crore.

title: Beardo nears Rs 300 Cr revenue in FY26; profit jumps 70%
summary:
Marico-owned men's grooming brand Beardo reported a strong financial performance in FY26, with revenue nearing the Rs 300 crore mark and improving profitability by 70%  during the fiscal year.

According to its standalone financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC), revenue from operations rose 40% to Rs 299 crore in FY26 from Rs 214 crore in FY25. 

The company's entire operating revenue came from the sale of products, with domestic sales contributing 99% and exports accounting for the remaining 1%.
The Ahmedabad-based company also recorded Rs 1 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 300 crore in FY26.
Coming to expenses, in line with the company's scale, material consumption, its largest cost, increased 36% to Rs 128 crore. Advertising and promotional spend jumped 59.6% to Rs 83 crore as the company stepped up investments to drive sales and strengthen brand visibility, while employee benefit expenses rose 30.2% to Rs 18.3 crore.
Other overheads like transportation cost, legal & professional, travelling pushed the overall expenses by 37% to Rs 270 crore.
Higher advertising and marketing spend helped Beardo drive a 40% increase in revenue, which, coupled with operating efficiencies, lifted its profit after tax (PAT) by 70% to Rs 22.12 crore in FY26 from Rs 13 crore a year earlier.

On a unit level, the company spent Rs 0.90 to earn one rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Beardo's EBITDA margin improved to 10.57% in FY26 from 9.17% in FY25, while its ROCE stood at 66.52% during the fiscal year ending March 2026.
On the balance sheet front, total assets increased to Rs 126 crore from Rs 72 crore in FY25, while current assets stood at Rs 115 crore, compared to Rs 60 crore in the previous fiscal.
In the men's grooming and D2C personal care segment, Beardo competes with The Man Company, which reported Rs 161 crore in revenue in FY26 while widening its losses to Rs 33 crore. Bombay Shaving Company, meanwhile, posted a 2.4X jump in revenue to Rs 635 crore and reported its first-ever positive adjusted EBITDA of Rs 2 crore. Another key rival, VLCC-owned Ustraa, is yet to file its FY26 financial statements.
Marico kicked off 2026 with two acquisitions. In January, it acquired a 93.27% stake in gourmet snacking brand 4700BC from PVR INOX, followed by the purchase of a 60% majority stake in plant-based protein supplements brand Cosmix in February.

title: Lighthouse Canton closes Rs 1,050 Mn private credit investment in Emerald Leisures
summary:
Lighthouse Canton, a global investment firm with over $6 billion in assets under management, has closed a Rs 1,050 million private credit investment in Emerald Leisures Limited through its India based Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), the LC Luminere Credit Fund, and affiliated entities.
Emerald Leisures is a BSE listed leisure and hospitality company that owns and operates Club Emerald, a multi sport, hospitality and recreational destination in Mumbai.
The investment will provide long term capital to support Emerald Leisures' growth plans. Structured as secured non convertible debentures, the facility is backed by the company's operating cash flows and supported by collateral, escrowed cash flows, promoter support and identified liquidity events.
The transaction adds to Lighthouse Canton's private credit portfolio in India, where it provides structured financing solutions to established businesses. Through its India private credit platform, the firm offers capital solutions tailored to the financing requirements of businesses across sectors.
Lighthouse Canton manages assets for ultra high net worth individuals, family offices, institutional investors and global investors. Its investment capabilities span private credit, growth debt, venture capital, real estate private equity, public equities and global macro hedge fund strategies.
The firm's private credit platform is supported by an origination network with access to more than 500 issuer relationships and over 1,000 promoter families, providing a pipeline of proprietary investment opportunities across sectors.

title: Freshworks turns profitable with $237 Mn revenue in Q2 CY26
summary:
Nasdaq-listed SaaS firm Freshworks reported a 16% year-on-year increase in revenue to $237.4 million in the second quarter ended June 2026, while achieving its first quarterly GAAP profitability this year. 
The company posted a GAAP net profit of $3.2 million in Q2 CY26, compared to a net loss of $1.7 million in the corresponding quarter last year. Operating income stood at $6.1 million, against an operating loss of $8.7 million a year earlier.  
According to the filing, non-GAAP operating income grew to $55.9 million, translating into a 23.6% operating margin, compared to 21.9% in the year ago quarter.  
For Freshworks, sales and marketing costs rose nearly 12% to $106.5 million from $95.2 million in Q2 CY26, while research and development expenses increased to $43.8 million from $39.9 million. General and administrative expenses declined to $37.9 million from $47 million, although the company incurred $7 million in restructuring charges during the quarter. 
Total operating expenses increased to $195.2 million from $182.2 million. 
The company generated $58.5 million in operating cash flow and $57.7 million in adjusted free cash flow during the quarter. Cash & cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities stood at $665.3 million as of June 30, 2026.  
Freshworks also continued to expand its enterprise customer base. The number of customers contributing more than $100,000 in annual recurring revenue (ARR) rose 25% year-on-year to 1,746, while customers contributing over $50,000 in ARR increased 18% to 4,091. Net dollar retention rate stood at 104%. 
Freshworks raised its full-year guidance and now expects CY26 revenue between $963.5 million and $966.5 million, with non-GAAP operating income projected at $222 million to $228 million.

title: C2C marketplace Vingo raises Rs 10 Cr seed round led by IndiaQuotient
summary:
Vingo, a consumer-to-consumer marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned products, has raised Rs 10 crore ($1 million) in a seed funding round led by IndiaQuotient. Inuka Capital and Credgenics founder Rishabh Goel also participated in the round.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen its product, invest in trust and payment infrastructure, study user behaviour and support marketing across key user groups.
Founded in March 2026 by Parth Sarthi, Saransh Goyal and Krish Vashistha, Vingo enables users to buy and sell pre-owned products directly. The platform currently operates in Bengaluru and is available on Android and iOS.
Vingo combines identity verification, community-based product discovery, escrow-backed payments and bidding to address trust issues between buyers and sellers. Its categories include smartphones, cameras, gaming consoles, musical instruments, fashion and sports equipment.
As per market research, India's recommerce market is projected to grow from $5.91 billion in 2026 to $8.61 billion by 2030. Vingo plans to focus on the C2C segment as it expands its platform and user base.

title: Personal assistance startup Hulp secures $2.6 Mn seed funding
summary:
Personal assistance and concierge platform Hulp has raised $2.6 million (around Rs 25 crore) in a seed funding round co-led by Sparrow Capital and BITKRAFT Ventures, with participation from DeVC (Z47) and angel investors, including PB Fintech co-founder and chairman Yashish Dahiya.
The proceeds will be used to expand AI workflows across lifestyle, household, and operational management, strengthen the senior leadership team, and enhance the company's technology and product capabilities, Hulp said in a press release.
Founded in April this year by Tarun Mathur, Neha Kulwal, and Vishal Singh Khutel, Hulp operates a personal assistance and concierge platform for urban households. The platform enables users to delegate daily, weekly, monthly, and one-time tasks across more than 15 categories through dedicated personal assistants supported by AI coordinated operations.
Before launching Hulp, Mathur was co-founder and chief business officer at PolicyBazaar (PB Fintech), where he led several of the company's business verticals.
According to the company, users can assign tasks through WhatsApp or its mobile app using voice notes. The platform offers services across categories such as government documentation, kitchen management, runner services, laundry, gardening, event bookings, restaurant reservations, and travel.
The Gurugram-based startup currently operates in Delhi, Gurugram, and Noida, and plans to expand to Mumbai, Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, and Chennai. It says it is supported by a 50-member operations team that manages routine household and lifestyle tasks.

title: InRisk Labs raises $27 Mn in Series A round led by Bessemer, Northpoint Capital
summary:
Technology-led risk and reinsurance platform InRisk Labs has raised $27 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Northpoint Capital.
The funding comes alongside a regulatory milestone for the company. Its subsidiary, EarthRe Insurance IFSC Limited, has received a licence from the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) to operate as a reinsurer. The company said EarthRe is the first incorporated reinsurer to receive a licence from the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) at GIFT City.
The fresh capital will be deployed to strengthen underwriting, actuarial, catastrophe modelling and AI capabilities, expand into natural catastrophe and climate risk as well as other non life segments including marine cargo and motor, develop parametric and structured reinsurance products, and meet regulatory capital requirements for scaling EarthRe’s operations in India’s $10 billion reinsurance market.
The company said the licence marks its transition from a technology led insurtech platform to an integrated reinsurance group with licensed risk bearing capacity. While InRisk Labs will continue to build technology, data and risk intelligence infrastructure, EarthRe will underwrite reinsurance business through its regulated balance sheet.
EarthRe is focused on non life reinsurance across natural catastrophe, climate risk, property, crop and specialty lines. The company said its platform integrates climate, geospatial, satellite, exposure and claims data to improve underwriting, pricing, portfolio construction and capital allocation. It also plans to offer treaty, facultative, structured and parametric reinsurance products designed for India and other Global South markets.
“India will be the most consequential insurance market over the next two decades. To drive sustainable growth, we must build indigenous capacity and tailored solutions built by India, for India,” said Malay Kumar Poddar, chief executive officer of EarthRe.
Vishal Gupta, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, said the firm backed the company at the seed stage and has now doubled down on its investment, while Sameer Brij Verma, founder and CIO of Northpoint Capital, said EarthRe combines a licensed balance sheet with an AI native risk platform and deep underwriting expertise.

title: Deep-tech energy startup Adiabatic Technologies raises Rs 8.3 Cr in seed round
summary:
Deep-tech energy startup Adiabatic Technologies has raised Rs 8.3 crore in a seed funding round co-led by Malpani Ventures and Avinya Ventures, with participation from Appreciate Capital, DeVC, Operators Studio, and UPES Incubator.
The company had previously raised Rs 1.1 crore in an angel funding round from Soonicorn Ventures and other investors in November last year.
The fresh proceeds will be used to expand its manufacturing capacity to 100 MWh annually, accelerate product development, strengthen its engineering team, and scale deployment of its battery systems across robotics, defence, and other sectors, Adiabatic said in a press release.
Founded in 2022 by Darshan Meher, Adiabatic develops custom lithium ion battery packs, smart chargers, and proprietary Battery Management Systems (BMS) for OEMs operating in high reliability industries. The company says it has deployed more than 20,000 battery systems across over 25 OEMs serving sectors such as robotics, defence, drones, agriculture equipment, electric vehicles, and solar energy.
According to the Pune-based startup, it designs its battery systems in house, covering cell selection, pack architecture, thermal management, and its proprietary Battery Management System. Its products are built for applications requiring high discharge performance, fast charging, intelligent battery management, and thermal safety.
The company plans to focus on specialised battery platforms for robotics, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), industrial automation, unmanned aerial systems, and other applications where reliability and performance are critical.
Adiabatic competes with startups such as EMO Energy, Clean Energy, Neuron Energy, and Inverted Energy.

title: Peak XV, Elevation Capital sell 2.27% stake in Meesho for Rs 1,949 Cr via block deals
summary:
Meesho's early investors Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital on Tuesday divested a combined 2.27% stake in the e-commerce marketplace through block deals on the NSE worth Rs 1,949.28 crore.
According to exchange data, both investors offloaded 5.24 crore shares each at Rs 186 apiece, taking the total shares sold to 10.48 crore.
The shares were acquired by a mix of domestic and global institutional investors. Axis Mutual Fund and Fidelity emerged among the largest buyers in the transaction.
Other participants included UTI Mutual Fund, HSBC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company, Franklin Templeton Mutual Fund, Edelweiss Mutual Fund, Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore Pte, Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, Prudential Hong Kong, Societe Generale, BNP Paribas Financial Markets, Ashoka WhiteOak funds, Ghisallo Master Fund LP, India Acorn Fund, Susquehanna Pacific Pty Ltd, NRSGVCC and several other institutional investors.
As of June 2026, Elevation Capital and Peak XV Partners held 12.04% and 10.06% stakes in Meesho, respectively. Following the block deal, Elevation Capital pared nearly 9.4% of its holding, while Peak XV Partners reduced around 9.9% of its stake.
The transaction comes weeks after Meesho reported a strong June quarter. The company posted a 48% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 3,713 crore in Q1 FY27, while its net loss narrowed 54% to Rs 133 crore from Rs 289 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.
At the end of Tuesday's trading session, Meesho’ shares were priced at Rs 191.88, taking the company's market capitalization to Rs 88,750 crore (around $9.34 billion).

title: OfBusiness doubles exports to Rs 2,500 Cr in FY26
summary:
Small and medium enterprise focused supply chain and financing platform OfBusiness' exports more than doubled to over Rs 2,500 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026, accounting for 12% of its consolidated revenue, according to a company press release. 
The Gurugram-based firm attributed the export growth partly to global buyers diversifying sourcing away from China. It said India's growing position as a manufacturing and sourcing base has supported demand across its apparel and food processing businesses. 
According to the release, the company now exports to more than 70 countries, including the US, the UK, the EU, and Japan. It expects exports to grow further in FY27. The company said the recently implemented India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement will support this growth by removing tariffs on nearly 99% of Indian export lines entering the UK, including textiles and apparel. 
The US remains OfBusiness' largest export market, the company said. In apparel, it supplies seven of the world's top 10 apparel retailers. The company is also expanding sourcing and manufacturing capacity in Bangladesh while increasing its manufacturing footprint across India.
Exports from its food processing business, which ships products from Karnataka to the US, Canada, the EU and Australia, are expected to double again in FY27. Towards the end of FY26, OfBusiness also started exporting bulk chemicals to South Asia and the Middle East.
"Winning global customers today takes more than competitive pricing. It demands vertical integration, consistent quality, traceability and reliable execution," said Asish Mohapatra, cofounder and CEO of OfBusiness. 
OfBusiness reported consolidated revenue of Rs 20,645 crore and profit after tax of Rs 724 crore for FY26. Its commerce business generated Rs 19,174 crore in revenue with EBITDA of Rs 769 crore, while operating cash flow stood at Rs 1,302 crore. The company also reported positive free cash flow of Rs 390 crore during the fiscal year. Entrackr had exclusively reported OfBusiness financial numbers last month.

title: Govt Bill signals return of MDR on UPI
summary:
The Centre on Tuesday introduced the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha, proposing changes to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 that would give the government the flexibility to decide which electronic payment modes remain exempt from merchant charges, including merchant discount rate (MDR).
The proposed amendment removes the existing reference to the Income tax Act from provisions related to electronic payment modes and empowers the Central Government to notify one or more electronic payment modes on which banks and payment system providers cannot levy charges.
The Bill does not impose MDR on UPI or any other digital payment mode. Instead, it allows the government to decide through future notifications which payment modes will continue to remain free of charges and which may attract charges.
The move is likely to revive discussions around the zero MDR regime, a long standing demand from banks and payment companies that have argued the current framework makes it difficult to recover payment processing costs.
The development comes more than a year after Entrackr reported that the Finance Ministry and the Reserve Bank of India were considering allowing MDR on UPI transactions for large merchants. The Finance Ministry had denied the report at the time, saying there was no proposal under consideration. 
According to ANI, the payment related changes are part of the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which also proposes amendments to the Income tax Act, 2025 and the Finance Act, 2026, while replacing the Income tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026.
The Bill also proposes extending tax incentives for electronics manufacturing until March 31, 2041, easing compliance requirements for offshore investment funds, and providing tax exemptions for certain foreign investors and the diamond trade.

title: Nykaa’s profits jump 3.3X to Rs 80 Cr in Q1 FY27; acquires 51% stake in skin care brand Aminu
summary:
Online beauty and fashion platform Nykaa announced its Q1 FY27 results today. The company reported a 29% year-on-year increase in operating revenue, while profit surged 3.3X to Rs 80 crore during the quarter.
According to its financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE), revenue from operations rose to Rs 2,782 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,155 crore in the year-ago quarter.

The beauty segment remained the company's largest business, contributing over 90% of operating revenue at Rs 2,516 crore, while the fashion segment added Rs 253 crore, accounting for around 9% of the total.
For Nykaa, Cost of materials remained Nykaa's largest expense, accounting for 57% of total expenditure at Rs 1,506 crore in Q1 FY27. Employee benefit expenses rose over 23% to Rs 225 crore, while finance, marketing, technology, and other overheads pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 2,662 crore during the quarter.
Strong revenue growth and better cost efficiencies helped Nykaa post a 3.3X jump in profit to Rs 80 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 24 crore in the year-ago quarter.  Sequentially, the firm’s profit remained flat compared to Rs 79 crore in the previous quarter.
Separately, Nykaa approved the acquisition of a 51% stake in Aminu Wellness Private Limited for up to Rs 32 crore in cash. Incorporated in 2019, Aminu Wellness manufactures and sells skincare products. It had a turnover of Rs 19.4 crore in FY26.
Nykaa said the acquisition will strengthen its presence in the premium beauty and personal care segment by adding Aminu's R&D capabilities and omnichannel distribution network.
At the close of Tuesday's trading session, Nykaa's shares were priced at Rs 342.5, taking the company's market capitalization to Rs 98,088 crore (around $10.3 billion).

title: Zoppler Systems raises Rs 6.5 Cr from Finvolve and India Accelerator
summary:
Defence and dual use technology company Zoppler Systems has raised Rs 6.5 crore in a funding round co-led by Finvolve and India Accelerator (IA).
The proceeds will be used to accelerate product development, strengthen field validation of indigenous technologies, expand engineering capabilities, and scale deployments across defence and dual use sectors, Zoppler Systems said in a press release.
Co-founded in November 2024 by Om Rana, Prakash Ramachandra, and Shridhar YB, Zoppler Systems develops indigenous RF sensing products and a vendor agnostic decision and autonomy platform. Its technology integrates sensing, intelligence, and response across localized and networked deployments, with applications spanning airborne, ground, naval, and future space domains.
Powered by Edge AI, Zoppler's open architecture enables defence organisations to enhance compatible existing systems with advanced sensing, decision intelligence, and response capabilities without replacing legacy infrastructure.
The Bengaluru-based startup supports both localized and networked autonomy, enabling multiple assets to share intelligence and coordinate mission critical responses across diverse operational environments.
According to the company, its platform is designed to enable faster decision making, greater operational flexibility, and seamless interoperability without requiring customers to replace compatible existing infrastructure. Beyond defence, it also sees dual use applications across critical infrastructure, ports, airports, energy, industrial facilities, and logistics, where real time sensing and intelligent decision making are becoming increasingly important.

title: MapMyIndia reports Rs 140 Cr revenue and Rs 50.4 Cr profit in Q1 FY27

According to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE), revenue from operations rose to Rs 139.7 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 121.6 crore in the year-ago quarter.

MapMyIndia is a deep-tech company that provides digital maps, geospatial software, location-based APIs, IoT solutions, and mapping platforms to enterprises, automakers, government agencies, developers, and consumers.
MapMyIndia serves customers across automotive, enterprise, and government segments, offering mapping and geospatial solutions to automakers, businesses, and public sector organizations.
Revenue from map data and related services, including royalties, subscriptions, software, and projects, remained the company's largest revenue stream at Rs 114 crore, largely flat year-on-year. Meanwhile, revenue from hardware device sales more than tripled to Rs 23.1 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 7.6 crore in the year-ago quarter.
MapMyIndia also made Rs 19.65 crore from non-operating sources, which pushed its total income in the quarter to Rs 159.4 crore. Sequentially, overall income declined marginally by 2% from Rs 162.8 crore in Q4 FY26.
Employee benefit expenses remained the company's largest cost, accounting for over 27% of total expenditure. The expense stood flat at Rs 25.6 crore, followed by material costs of Rs 21.7 crore and technical services outsourced expenses of Rs 13.3 crore.

title: Capillary Technologies’ revenue grows 43% to Rs 257 Cr in Q1 FY27
summary:
SaaS firm Capillary Technologies announced its financial results for Q1 FY27 today, reporting a 42.6% year-on-year increase in revenue. However, the company slipped into losses during the quarter after reporting a Rs 33.4 crore exceptional loss related to a cyber-enabled banking fraud at its Czech Republic subsidiary.
The Bengaluru-based company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 256.6 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 179.9 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statement sourced from BSE.

Founded in 2008 by Aneesh Reddy, Krishna Mehra, and Ajay Modani, Capillary Technologies offers cloud-native loyalty, CRM, and customer engagement solutions to more than 465 brands across 53 countries. Its clientele includes Tata Digital, Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail, and Abbott Laboratories.
The company earned Rs 242.4 crore from subscription services, which contributed 94.5% of its operating revenue, while installation and campaign services brought in the remaining Rs 12.2 crore. It also reported Rs 5.7 crore as other income, which took its total income to Rs 262.3 crore in Q1 FY27.
On a quarterly basis, the firm’s operating revenue grew 34% from Rs 191 crore in Q4 FY26.
Employee benefits remained the company's largest expense, rising 40% year-on-year to Rs 119.8 crore and accounting for more than half of its total expenditure. Software and server charges stood at Rs 45 crore, while professional and consultancy fees came in at Rs 34 crore. Overall, total expenses increased 31.6% to Rs 237.5 crore during the quarter.
In the end, the company slipped into the red during the quarter due to a Rs 33.4 crore exceptional charge related to a cyber-enabled banking fraud at its Czech Republic subsidiary. Its adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 44 crore.
As of 2:10 PM today, shares of Capillary Technologies rose over 15% to Rs 571, taking its total market capitalization to Rs 4,539 crore (about $477 million).

Generative artificial intelligence startup Simplismart is set to raise nearly Rs 97 crore (around $9 million) in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from existing investors Accel India and Shastra VC, as well as new investor Micromax Informatics.
The board of Simplismart has approved a resolution to issue 12,100 CCPS at an issue price of Rs 37 lakh each to raise the capital, according to its regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr.
Dallas Venture Capital will invest Rs 44.84 crore, followed by Accel India with Rs 24.09 crore. Shastra VC will infuse Rs 22.24 crore, while Micromax Informatics will invest Rs 5.19 crore. Tarusa Capital and Simraan Teckchandani will also participate in the round with investments of Rs 37 lakh each.
According to Entrackr's estimates, the Bengaluru-based company will be valued at around Rs 826 crore post allotment. The fresh capital will be used to support the company's long term growth plans, including business expansion, working capital requirements, and other general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2022 by former Oracle and Google engineers Amritanshu Jain and Devansh Ghatak, Simplismart develops AI infrastructure software that enables enterprises to deploy, manage, and optimize production grade AI models without writing code. Its inference-first platform improves GPU utilization and reduces inference costs across workloads such as large language models (LLMs), vision language models, speech recognition, and image and video generation. 
The startup counts Tata 1mg, Mindtickle, InVideo, and Dashtoon among its customers, and has partnered with Nvidia to make its AI inference platform available on the chipmaker's infrastructure.
In May 2026, The Economic Times reported that Nvidia was in talks to lead a $20 million funding round in Simplismart. Previously, it raised $7 million in October 2024.
Following the allotment, Accel India will remain the company's largest institutional shareholder with a 19.92% stake. Dallas Venture Capital and Shastra VC Fund II will hold 6.23% and 2.69%, respectively, while Micromax Informatics will own 0.63% of the company.
The company is yet to generate significant operating revenue. Its operating revenue doubled to Rs 1.22 crore in FY25 from Rs 61 lakh in FY24, while its losses widened to Rs 9.02 crore from Rs 67 lakh in the previous fiscal.

title: Mintoak acquires loyalty and rewards tech company ICC Loyalty

ICC Loyalty provides loyalty and rewards technology to more than 30 banks. Its platform enables financial institutions to offer personalised rewards, targeted campaigns and lifecycle engagement programmes aimed at improving customer retention and transaction frequency. The company serves over 11 million customers across more than 10 countries.
According to the company, the acquisition expands Mintoak's capabilities beyond merchant payments and value added services to include customer engagement, loyalty and rewards. It also enables banks to serve both acquiring and issuing businesses through a unified platform.
The combined business generates more than $30 million in annual revenue with a profitability margin exceeding 30%, according to the company. It said the combined platform will enable banks to connect merchants, consumers and payment data to improve customer engagement and create additional revenue opportunities.
Following the acquisition, Mintoak now partners with more than 50 banks across over 20 countries, including HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and SBI Payments in India, Emirates Islamic and RAKBANK in the Middle East, and Absa Bank in Africa. Backed by investors including PayPal Ventures, British International Investment, Pravega Ventures, HDFC Bank and Z3Partners, the company says its platform supports over 5 million merchants and 11 million customers while processing more than $93 billion in annual payment volume.
Mintoak said the acquisition will help it expand its payments and engagement platform for banks across emerging markets as financial institutions increasingly look beyond transaction processing to strengthen customer relationships and diversify revenue streams.

summary:
Shares of electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy rallied nearly 18% on Tuesday, touching an all-time high of Rs 1,500 apiece, as brokerages remained bullish following the company's strong Q1 FY27 performance. The stock had closed at Rs 1,272.7 in the previous session.
The sharp rally came a day after Ather reported robust growth across revenue, margins and profitability, reinforcing investor confidence in the company's growth trajectory. Strong demand for its electric scooters, improving operating leverage, a recent funding boost and expectations around new product launches also boosted sentiment.
For the quarter ended June 2026, Ather's revenue from operations grew 89% year-on-year to Rs 1,217 crore, while consolidated total income rose 87.2% to Rs 1,260 crore. The company also reported a sharp improvement in profitability, with net loss narrowing to Rs 51 crore from Rs 178 crore in the year-ago quarter. 
Consolidated EBITDA turned positive at Rs 9 crore against a loss of Rs 106 crore in Q1 FY26, while EBITDA margin improved by 1,650 basis points to 0.8%. 
Ather delivered 83,173 electric scooters during the quarter, while customer enquiries rose 95% to 7.07 lakh and pre-orders surged 158% to 1.5 lakh, indicating demand continued to outpace production. The company also said its AURIC plant remains on track to begin production in Q3 FY27, with the first scooter on the new EL platform set to debut on August 29.
Brokerages remained bullish on Ather. CLSA retained its 'Outperform' rating with a target price of Rs 1,600, citing strong volume growth, robust bookings, upcoming capacity expansion and the EL platform launch. It also noted that demand continues to outpace production capacity.
HSBC maintained its 'Buy' rating and raised its target price to Rs 1,450, highlighting better-than-expected margins driven by lower operating costs and expecting market share gains as new capacity comes online. Nomura also retained its 'Buy' rating with the high target price of Rs 1,714, calling Ather its preferred electric two-wheeler stock, backed by strong execution, brand strength, and sustained growth prospects.
Brokerages said Ather's improving unit economics, rising contribution from software and services, upcoming capacity expansion and new product pipeline position the company well for sustained growth, prompting a broad re-rating of the stock.
As at 11:37 PM (today), Ather’s shares were  trading at Rs 1,463.9, valuing the company at Rs 57,349 crore or around $6 billion.

title: Agentic AI startup Kily raises Rs 30 Cr in round led by Sorin Investments
summary:
Agentic enterprise AI startup Kily has raised Rs 30 crore ($3.1 million) in a funding round led by Sorin Investments, with participation from Razorpay and Wyser Capital.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its product capabilities, expand go-to-market operations and increase adoption among consumer brands in India.
Founded in 2025 by Sankalp Mehrotra, Anurag Singh and Sharad Chitlangia, Kily develops AI agents that help brands and sellers manage operations across e-commerce and quick commerce platforms.
Its platform collects marketplace data and combines it with a brand's business goals and operating requirements to automate decisions and workflows. It helps brands manage areas such as product visibility, advertising, pricing, inventory and other commerce operations across digital platforms.
Kily works across e-commerce and quick commerce platforms including Amazon, Flipkart, Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart. Since its launch, the startup has worked with consumer brands including ITC.
According to Kily, its AI agents are designed to reduce the use of spreadsheets, dashboards and manual processes by automating commerce management and decision-making.

title: Former Swiggy, Zomato executives launch AI startup Profound with $1.5 Mn seed round
summary:
Bengaluru based AI startup Profound has raised $1.5 million in a seed funding round as it launched an AI powered platform for professional networking and hiring.
The startup was founded by Anuj Rathi and Prashant Parashar, former product and technology leaders with experience across Swiggy, Zomato, Cleartrip, Flipkart, Ola and Walmart Labs.
The seed round saw participation from angel investors including Swiggy CEO Sriharsha Majety, Swiggy cofounder Nandan Reddy, former Zomato cofounder Pankaj Chaddah, Razorpay CEO Harshil Mathur, WhatsApp Global Head Kunal Shah, and OfBusiness cofounder Bhuvan Gupta, along with venture capital firms Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital.
The company will use the fresh capital to expand its engineering and product teams, enhance its AI capabilities, and develop its matching and introductions engine. It plans to onboard one million professionals globally before opening beta access to more users.
Profound offers every professional an AI powered representative that starts with a voice conversation to understand a user's experience, expertise, work style and career goals. Based on this, the platform recommends opportunities and facilitates professional introductions.
The startup also enables hiring managers to create AI representatives for roles and teams, allowing companies to capture hiring requirements through voice conversations instead of traditional job descriptions.
"Just as actors have agents and athletes have managers, Profound gives each professional their own AI Rep," cofounder and CEO Anuj Rathi said in a statement.
The company has opened early access for its first cohort, while a wider beta launch is planned later this year.

title: Tractor Junction gets RBI licence to launch NBFC arm Dhanrise Finance
summary:
Rural auto fintech platform Tractor Junction has received a Certificate of Registration from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to operate a non banking financial company (NBFC) through its wholly owned arm, Dhanrise Finance Private Limited.
The company said Dhanrise has received a Type II NBFC ND ICC licence and will start lending operations in October 2026, beginning with Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh. It plans to expand to Gujarat, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Uttar Pradesh in phases.
According to Tractor Junction, Dhanrise will focus on financing used tractors and rural vehicles, targeting an estimated Rs 50,000 crore credit gap in the segment. The company aims to disburse Rs 100 crore in loans over the first 24 months, with typical loan sizes ranging from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh.
The company said it will use AI based valuation, computer vision driven condition assessment, satellite imagery and a 120 point tractor inspection framework to reduce loan approval time from 8 to 10 days to less than 24 hours. It will leverage Tractor Junction’s network of over 6 crore annual platform visitors, retail operations across 100 cities in six states and its fintech arm FINJ, which facilitates about Rs 350 crore in rural vehicle loans every month through over 30,000 channel partners. 
“India has more than ten dedicated used car financiers, but not a single institutional used tractor specialist, even though the unmet credit need is Rs 50,000 crore,” said Rajat Gupta, CEO and Founder of Tractor Junction. 
The regulatory approval comes after Tractor Junction reported revenue of Rs 198.4 crore in FY26, a 62% increase from the previous year. The company said it is on track to reach Rs 400 crore in revenue in FY27. In November 2025, it raised Rs 200 crore ($22.6 million) in a Series A funding round led by Astanor, with participation from existing investors Info Edge and Omnivore.

title: Nazara’s Q1 FY27 results hit by associate losses and impairment; Nitish Mittersain steps down as CEO
summary:
Nazara Technologies, a gaming and sports media company, reported a 14% year on year decline in operating revenue during the first quarter of FY27. The company also slipped into a loss during the quarter.
This is a rare quarterly loss for Nazara, which last reported a net loss of Rs 34 crore in Q2 FY26 following a write off related to its investment in PokerBaazi after the enactment of the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025.
Nazara’s operating revenue declined to Rs 429 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 499 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange.
Gaming remained the company’s largest revenue contributor, accounting for 60.4% of operating revenue. Revenue from the segment grew 14.1% year on year to Rs 275 crore from Rs 241 crore in the same quarter last year. Meanwhile, esports revenue declined 81.8% to Rs 28 crore, while ad tech revenue increased 18.9% to Rs 126 crore.
Including Rs 9 crore in other income, Nazara’s total income stood at Rs 438 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 576 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.
On the expense front, total expenditure declined 12.7% to Rs 455 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 521 crore in Q1 FY26. Advertising and business promotion remained the largest cost at Rs 153 crore, followed by employee benefits at Rs 82 crore and content, event and web server expenses at Rs 63 crore.
Nazara slipped into a net loss of Rs 82 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to a net profit of Rs 51 crore in the same quarter last year. The loss included Rs 62 crore as the company’s share of losses from associates and a Rs 22 crore impairment loss.
On a sequential basis, operating revenue grew 7.8% from Rs 398 crore in Q4 FY26 to Rs 429 crore in Q1 FY27, while the company swung from a net profit of Rs 55.7 crore in the previous quarter to a net loss.
At the close of trading on Monday, Nazara Technologies' shares settled at Rs 339.55, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately Rs 12,568 crore ($1.32 billion).
In a separate filing, the board appointed Raymond Albaladejo Stauffer as CEO, effective September 1, 2026. Founder Nitish Mittersain stepped down as CEO and will continue as Managing Director, focusing on long term strategy and strategic partnerships.

title: MakeMyTrip reports $286 Mn revenue in Q1 FY27; profit plunges 65%
summary:
Online travel platform MakeMyTrip reported a mixed performance for the first quarter of FY27, with revenue growing in single digits while profit declined 65% to $9.1 million due to higher finance costs linked to its convertible notes.
The Nasdaq-listed company recorded 6.2% year-on-year growth in revenue to $285.6 million in the quarter ended June 2026 from $268.8 million in the corresponding period last year. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 16.1%.
MakeMyTrip said the quarter was affected by a more than 10% depreciation in the Indian rupee against the U.S. dollar, as well as subdued international outbound travel due to the ongoing West Asia conflict. However, strong domestic travel demand helped offset part of the impact.
Hotels and packages remained the company's largest business with revenue of $151.2 million, recording a 6.7% year-on-year increase. Bus ticketing revenue climbed 15.9% to $44.9 million. Revenue from the air ticketing segment fell 7.5% to $55.6 million, while the others segment recorded 19.6% growth to $33.9 million.
Gross bookings grew 9.4% to $2.85 billion, led by growth across hotels, bus ticketing and air travel. Hotel room nights rose nearly 20% to 12.8 million, while bus ticket volumes increased 23.9% to 43.6 million.
On the expense front, service costs rose 10.4% year-on-year to $82.7 million, driven by strong demand for packages and car bookings in India. Marketing and sales promotion expenses increased 11.1% to $48.8 million, while other operating expenses edged up 2.3% to $65.3 million. Personnel expenses, however, declined 3.4% to $38.8 million.
Finance costs surged to $35 million in Q1 FY27 from $10.8 million a year earlier, primarily due to higher interest expenses on convertible senior notes. As a result, net finance costs jumped to $28.3 million from $4 million in the year-ago quarter.
In the end, the Gurugram-based company reported a 64.7% decline in profit to $9.1 million during the quarter, as higher finance costs weighed on its bottom line. Its Adjusted EBITDA stood at $55.5 million during the quarter.
As of June 30, 2026, MakeMyTrip held $370.7 million in cash and cash equivalents and $423.6 million in term deposits.

title: Beyond earnings: Pine Labs rewrites POS playbook, bets on Blinkit and Zepto for gift cards
summary:
While investors focused on Pine Labs' quarterly earnings and guidance, the company's first post-listing earnings call offered a deeper look at the strategy shaping its next phase of growth. Beyond the headline numbers, the fintech company disclosed a new economics for its POS business, revealed that its credit-processing business has quietly grown into a nearly Rs 100 crore annual revenue stream, and outlined plans to expand gift card distribution through Blinkit and Zepto. 
Management also shared updates on its AI initiatives, new issuing products and international expansion, providing fresh insight into how Pine Labs is evolving beyond its core payments business.
A new playbook for POS economics
Perhaps the biggest structural change outlined during the earnings call relates to Pine Labs' terminal business.
For years, the company purchased POS devices and leased them to merchants, earning recurring rental income. That model is now changing. Pine Labs said nearly 25-30% of new terminal deployments now require merchants to purchase the hardware upfront instead of the company carrying it on its own balance sheet.
While this lowers reported contribution margins because hardware sales are inherently low-margin, management said the strategy reduces depreciation, improves cash efficiency and creates a lighter balance sheet.
The company expects to deploy 125,000-130,000 terminals during the year, with most network investments already completed.
A Rs 100 Cr business hidden in plain sight 
Another notable disclosure was around Pine Labs' issuing platform.
Management revealed that its credit issuing and acquiring processing business has grown into an annual revenue business of nearly Rs 100 crore, a figure it has not previously highlighted publicly.
The company said its issuing platform today spans nearly 20 countries, extending well beyond gift cards into prepaid cards, forex cards and open-loop payment products.
To further expand the business, Pine Labs plans to launch meal cards, fuel cards and expense cards by October, while also building direct-to-consumer prepaid products.
Blinkit and Zepto become Pine Labs' new gift card storefronts
Pine Labs also revealed that it has started distributing gift cards through Blinkit and Zepto, signalling that quick commerce is becoming an important sales channel for digital gifting.
The company is simultaneously expanding into gaming by distributing Roblox gift cards and targeting in-app purchases, which management sees as another growth avenue.
Interestingly, despite multiple analyst questions on gift cards, issuing and distribution, management made no reference to breakage income, unredeemed gift cards or breakage accounting, instead focusing on processing, distribution and new products.
AI and global expansion power the next phase 
Alongside these strategic shifts, Pine Labs continued to outline its investments in AI and overseas markets.
The company said nearly 90% of new code across several business divisions is now written using AI-assisted tools, while it recently demonstrated what it called India's first agentic payment, where AI agents completed a payment transaction using UPI mandates.
Internationally, Pine Labs said it has won British Airways for its gift card platform, deployed 30,000 terminals with GCash in the Philippines and is expanding operations across Singapore and the UAE.
Despite reporting its first profitable year, Pine Labs continues to invest in growth, adding 500 sales employees over the past six months to strengthen merchant acquisition and enterprise sales. Notably, the company made no mention of engineering or technology hiring,
Taken together, the earnings call painted a picture of Pine Labs expanding beyond its core payments business through new POS economics, a growing issuing platform, AI investments and international expansion. Yet one aspect remained conspicuously absent. Despite extensive discussions around gift cards, issuing and processing, management made no reference to breakage income, unredeemed gift card balances or related accounting practices. Instead, the focus remained firmly on new distribution channels such as Blinkit and Zepto, processing capabilities and the launch of new prepaid products.

summary:
Used car retailing platform Spinny is preparing for its planned initial public offering (IPO) by converting into a public company.
The board has passed a special resolution to change the name of its parent entity from Valuedrive Technologies Private Limited to Valuedrive Technologies Limited, a move that typically precedes a public listing, according to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.
According to a recent Bloomberg report, Spinny has appointed Kotak, Morgan Stanley, and Citi as lead bankers for an IPO in CY27.
Founded in 2015 by Niraj Singh and Mohit Gupta, Spinny operates a full stack used car marketplace, offering vehicle buying, selling, financing, insurance, and after sales services. The company also owns Truebil and completed the acquisition of auto service platform GoMechanic in 2024. It further expanded its portfolio with the acquisition of Autocar India, an automotive media and car content platform, in March 2025.
According to sources, Spinny is currently selling close to 15,000 cars every month. The company serves car buyers across 25 cities and enables car sellers from more than 100 cities.
Sources also said Spinny plans to expand its buyer footprint to around 35 cities in the near term by adding 10 more locations.
For the fiscal year ended March 2025, Spinny's revenue from operations grew 25% year on year to Rs 4,657 crore from Rs 3,730 crore in FY24. According to sources, the company is expected to close FY26 with revenue of around Rs 6,000 crore.
Entrackr has reached out to Spinny for comments.
Spinny has raised approximately $780 million to date, with Tiger Global and Accel among its largest shareholders. The company last raised around $165 million from Accel Leaders Fund, Fidelity Investments, and other investors at a valuation of $1.5 billion to $1.8 billion.

title: Ather Energy reports Rs 1,217 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27, loss drops to Rs 51 Cr
summary:
Electric two-wheeler manufacturer Ather Energy announced its Q1 FY27 results today. During the period, the company reported 89% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue. At the same time, the losses for the Bengaluru-based company narrowed by 71% to Rs 51 crore.
Ather’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,217 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 645 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its quarterly report sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The sale of electric two-wheelers and related services remained Ather Energy's sole source of operating revenue, although the company did not disclose a detailed revenue breakup. During the quarter, it sold 88,655 vehicles, up 9% quarter-on-quarter from 81,072 units in Q4 FY26.
The company also recorded Rs 43 crore in other income, taking its total income for the quarter to Rs 1,260 crore.
Ather's largest expense continued to be the cost of materials, primarily battery cells and other components, which surged 88% year-on-year to Rs 977 crore in Q1 FY27 and accounted for nearly 75% of the company's total expenditure. Employee benefit expenses remained largely unchanged at Rs 118 crore during the quarter.
Depreciation and amortisation charges, along with spending on legal, advertising, and other operating expenses, pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 1,311 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 851 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Higher electric two-wheeler sales helped Ather significantly improve its bottom line during the quarter. The company more than doubled its vehicle sales to 88,655 units from 41,083 units in Q1 FY26, which contributed to a 71% decline in net loss to Rs 51 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 178 crore in the year-ago quarter.
According to Vahan data, Ather Energy retained its third position in July despite a 8.3% decline in registrations to 28,819 units and 14.89% market share.
Last month, Ather approved a Rs 1,200 crore preferential issue, with existing investor Hero MotoCorp committing nearly Rs 960 crore. The India-Japan Fund (IJF) will invest Rs 200 crore, while the company's promoters will contribute the remaining Rs 40 crore.
At the end of today’s trading session, Ather’s share price closed at Rs 1,280, with a total market capitalization of Rs 50,448 crore or $5.3 billion.

Founded in 2017 by Sunil Patel and Netaji Patro, Matel designs and manufactures motors, motor controllers, and integrated powertrains for automotive and industrial applications.
The startup offers solutions for a wide range of electric vehicles, including two wheelers, three wheelers, four wheelers, buses, and off road vehicles. It commenced mass production of its powertrains in April 2024 after receiving validation and certification from multiple EV OEMs.
Its products are used across electric vehicles, pumping and cooling systems, and other industrial applications.
The company has also developed magnet free motor technology and offers IE5 industrial motors, while an IE6 motor is under development. Matel currently supplies products to multiple OEMs across the two wheeler, three wheeler, and industrial segments.
Founder and CEO Sunil Patel previously led the Chetak EV development programme at Bajaj Auto's R&D division, while co founder Netaji Patro has held R&D roles at Maruti Suzuki and Bajaj Auto.

title: 1xBet branding reaches India via FanCode, Zee, Sony LIV; accountability remains unclear
summary:
Offshore betting platform 1xBet received prominent visibility during India's recent tour of Zimbabwe, streamed in India on FanCode and Zee. Its visibility raises questions over how 1xBet branding continues to reach Indian audiences despite multiple government advisories against advertisements for offshore betting and gambling platforms.
1xBet was an official partner of the three match T20 series held from July 23 to 26 at the Harare Sports Club. Its logo appeared on perimeter boards, sight screens, backdrops and other advertising spaces at the stadium.
The visibility comes against the backdrop of multiple government measures aimed at restricting the promotion of online money gaming and offshore betting platforms. Since 2022, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has issued multiple advisories asking television channels, digital publishers, OTT platforms and online intermediaries not to carry advertisements, including surrogate advertisements, for offshore betting and gambling platforms.
Separately, the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 was brought into force through a government notification issued in April this year, while the accompanying Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 took effect on May 1.
In its partnership announcement, 1xBet specifically highlighted the availability of the matches on FanCode and Zee Entertainment and said this would ensure broad brand exposure among the T20 audience.
Entrackr has reached out to 1xBet to understand whether reaching Indian audiences through FanCode and Zee was part of its sponsorship objective, whether it had any commercial arrangement with the platforms, and its position on the branding in light of India's online gaming and advertising regulations. The story will be updated if it responds.
The 1xBet branding was visible in the live broadcast and also appeared in match clips later posted by FanCode on its social media handles.
A person familiar with the matter at FanCode told Entrackr that the platform receives the feed directly from the publisher and has no control over advertisements displayed at the ground.
FanCode declined to comment on the story.
However, while FanCode may have limited control over branding embedded in a live feed supplied by the host broadcaster, the appearance of 1xBet branding in clips later posted on its own social media channels also brings into focus whether betting related branding can be reviewed, cropped, blurred or masked before such content is redistributed.
Entrackr has also reached out to Zee regarding the visibility of 1xBet branding during the series, its role, if any, in the sponsorship arrangement, and safeguards it follows for betting related branding in overseas sports feeds. The story will be updated if it responds.
Entrackr has asked the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting whether branding for offshore betting platforms embedded in overseas sports feeds falls within existing advertising restrictions when distributed in India, and whether Indian broadcasters and streaming platforms are expected to restrict or mask such branding. The story will be updated if the ministry responds.
Section 6 of the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 prohibits advertisements that directly or indirectly promote online money games. Entrackr has also sought clarity from the ministry on whether the provision has any bearing on branding for offshore betting platforms embedded in international sports broadcasts.
The legislation also affected India's online money gaming industry. Dream Sports, the parent company of FanCode, along with other real money gaming platforms such as Gameskraft, Zupee, WinZO and A23, discontinued paid contests after the law came into effect.
1xBet branding also visible on Sony LIV
A similar instance emerged during India A's recent tour of Sri Lanka, where 1xBet branding was prominently visible during matches broadcast in India on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.
Entrackr asked Sony whether it was aware of the branding, had any role in its broadcast, and what safeguards it has to restrict betting related advertisements in international feeds. Sony did not respond until the publication of this story.
The recurrence across two separate overseas tours suggests the issue is not limited to a single broadcast. It also puts the focus on the BCCI's role in overseas tours involving India and India A. While on ground advertising at overseas venues may be controlled by host boards and their commercial partners, it remains unclear whether the BCCI has guidelines or contractual safeguards concerning betting related sponsorships during matches involving Indian teams.
Entrackr reached out to the BCCI to understand its position on the 1xBet branding during both tours, whether it had raised the issue with the respective host boards, and whether it has any policy or contractual safeguards concerning betting related sponsorships during overseas tours involving Indian teams.
The BCCI did not respond until the publication of this story.
Even if stadium advertising is controlled by host boards or their commercial partners, broadcasters and streaming platforms redistribute the content to Indian audiences. The two instances raise questions over whether such platforms should review or mask betting related branding before it reaches viewers in India.

summary:
Logistics solutions firm LEAP India Limited has filed its red herring prospectus (RHP) with SEBI for its Rs 2,480 crore initial public offering (IPO), which is scheduled to open on August 7.
The IPO will open for subscription on August 7 and close on August 11, with the anchor book opening on August 6. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 151 to Rs 159 per share.
The company received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to launch its IPO in December last year.
According to its RHP, LEAP India has increased the fresh issue size to Rs 480 crore from the Rs 400 crore proposed in its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) filed in August last year. The remaining Rs 2,000 crore of the IPO comprises an offer for sale (OFS).

Founded in 2013, EAP India provides pallet pooling, container pooling, and related material-handling solutions across industries. The company counts leading FMCG, pharma, and e-commerce players among its clients.
JM Financial, Avendus Capital, IIFL Capital, and UBS Securities are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while MUFG Intime India is the registrar.
Of the proceeds from the fresh issue, Rs 360 crore will be used to repay certain borrowings, while the remaining amount will be allocated for general corporate purposes.
As of the RHP filing date, KKR-backed Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd. is the company's largest shareholder with a 73.78% stake, followed by founder Sunu Mathew, who holds 21.07%. Sixth Sense Ventures, First Bridge Fund, and Madhurima International Pvt. Ltd. own 1.41%, 1.21%, and 1%, respectively.

title: Snabbit crosses 115,000 daily jobs, says burn per job drops below Rs 250 in Q1 FY27
summary:
Quick home services startup Snabbit has crossed 115,000 fulfilled jobs in a single day, according to the company. It also reported improvements in its unit economics during the first quarter of FY27.
According to Snabbit, it completed around 4 million jobs in its core househelp category during Q1 FY27, while its consolidated Net Order Value (NOV), after accounting for customer discounts, crossed Rs 130. During the quarter, burn per job declined by more than Rs 100 quarter on quarter to below Rs 250.
The company scaled from around 400 daily jobs to more than 115,000 a day in under two years. It had crossed 50,000 daily jobs and one million monthly jobs earlier this year.
Snabbit currently operates across 10 cities including Mumbai, Delhi, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Gurgaon, Ghaziabad, Noida, Faridabad, Pune and Hyderabad, covering more than 150 micromarkets. According to the company, it continues to focus on increasing density within existing neighbourhoods to improve fulfilment efficiency and customer retention.
The company also reported early traction in newer categories such as Home Cooks and Salon at Home.
Founder and CEO Aayush Agarwal said that mature micromarkets are now completing more than 2,500 jobs a day, while several residential communities generate over 500 daily jobs. He added that the company expects its consolidated NOV to improve by another 15% to 20% over the coming months.
Snabbit currently facilitates more than 100,000 earning opportunities every day for its network of over 25,000 Experts and has enabled eShram registration for eligible workers on its platform.
The announcement comes months after Snabbit raised $56 million in a Series D funding round, taking its total capital raised to $112 million. 
The announcement comes amid growing competition in the quick home services segment. Rival Urban Company's InstaHelp also crossed 100,000 delivered orders in a single day on Sunday, reaching the milestone at 5:54 PM. The company said the final tally for the day was expected to be higher.
According to a recent Moneycontrol report, InstaHelp completed around 1.9 million orders in July, ahead of Snabbit's 1.85 million, while Pronto crossed 1.25 million bookings.
Snabbit also maintained that its growth has not been driven primarily by aggressive discounting. According to the company, its consolidated NOV crossed Rs 130 after customer discounts.

title: Urban Company’s InstaHelp crosses 100,000 daily delivered orders
summary:
Urban Company on Sunday announced that its quick service housekeeping vertical InstaHelp has crossed 100,000 delivered orders in a single day, around five months after the platform reached 50,000 daily bookings.
According to the company, InstaHelp crossed the 100,000 delivered orders milestone at 5:54 PM on August 2. The final number for the day is expected to be higher. The company added that the figure reflects peak daily deliveries, while the business will continue to focus on customer retention, service quality and the availability of service professionals for long term growth.
“Crossing 100,000 delivered orders in a single day, barely five months after we crossed 50,000, reflects both the growing consumer demand for InstaHelp and the strength of the operating model we've built. We are building this category the way we build everything at Urban Company with a strong focus on unit economics and long term value. As we scale, Net Transaction Value and contribution per order remain the metrics we hold ourselves to, because they reflect the true, durable health of the business,” said Abhiraj Singh Bhal, CEO and co-founder of Urban Company.
The announcement comes days after Urban Company disclosed its Q1 FY27 results. InstaHelp fulfilled 3.82 million orders during the quarter, up 43% from 2.67 million in Q4 FY26, while its adjusted EBITDA loss per order improved to Rs 346 from Rs 447 in the preceding quarter.
Urban Company launched InstaHelp as a pilot in Mumbai in March 2025. The platform offers housekeeping services such as cleaning, dishwashing, laundry and meal preparation, with professionals available within 10 to 15 minutes of booking. It currently operates across select micro markets in major metro cities.
In February this year, InstaHelp crossed 50,000 daily bookings, less than a year after its pilot launch. The company later said the platform completed more than 1 million monthly delivered bookings in March, with three days still left in the month.
According to a recent Moneycontrol report, InstaHelp completed around 1.9 million orders in July and regained the top position in the instant home services segment. Rival Snabbit completed around 1.85 million orders during the month, while Pronto crossed 1.25 million bookings.

title: Zepto confirms pre IPO private placement, says listing within SEBI approved timeline
summary:
Quick commerce major Zepto has officially confirmed that it will undertake a pre-IPO private placement ahead of its planned public listing, while indicating that it will continue to focus on business execution before launching its IPO.
In a statement issued on Friday, the company said it has agreed with major shareholders to close a pre IPO private placement of equity. The financing will strengthen its balance sheet, which stood at Rs 5,681 crore in cash with no debt as of March 31, 2026.
"As part of the IPO process, the Board and Founders have received terms from public market investors to list the company and are appreciative of the expressed interest. However, at this time, and afforded by the company's strong balance sheet, Zepto will focus on continued execution," the company said.
Zepto added that it will update its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with its operating results and financials in the coming quarters and intends to list within the timeframe permitted by SEBI under its approved UDRHP.
The announcement comes days after multiple media reports indicated that the company had postponed its IPO plans amid valuation discussions with investors. Reports had also suggested that Zepto was in talks to raise more than Rs 1,000 crore through a pre IPO placement from existing investors including Glade Brook, General Catalyst, Goodwater Capital, and Nexus Venture Partners.
Zepto had initially planned an IPO of around Rs 8,000 crore. In June, the company filed its updated DRHP with SEBI for a fresh issue of Rs 8,010 crore and subsequently received the regulator's approval. Recent reports had indicated that the company may reduce the IPO size to around Rs 5,000 crore to Rs 6,000 crore.
According to its FY26 financial statements, Zepto doubled its operating revenue to Rs 11,110 crore from Rs 5,454 crore in FY25. Its net loss, however, widened 26% to Rs 5,905 crore.
